definition: Restitution means restoration of something lost, or compensation paid for a loss or injury.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word restitution. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know restitution should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The judge ordered the con artist to pay full restitution to the retirees whose savings he had drained.
A refund is weaker than restitution, a refund simply returns the price you paid, while restitution makes up for the full loss a person actually suffered.
Reparations are stronger than restitution, restitution repays one victim for a specific loss, while reparations attempt to compensate entire groups for large-scale harm.

Compensation is any payment made to make up for a loss, injury, or inconvenience — insurance payouts, damages, even overtime pay. Restitution is the pointed version: restoring to a specific victim what they lost, or its full value, typically because the payer is answerable for the loss.

Repayment means giving back what is owed — settling a loan or a debt you took on. The money was always due. Restitution answers a loss rather than a debt: something was taken or destroyed, and its value is restored to the person who suffered the loss.

Redress is a remedy that sets a wrong right, and it can take almost any form — an apology, a policy change, a payment. Restitution is one specific kind of redress: restoring what was lost, or paying its value, to the person who was harmed.

After Theo accidentally knocked over and shattered Mrs.
Bell's antique porch lamp, he mowed her lawn every week that summer as restitution.
Theo cannot un-break the lamp, so he makes up for the loss with work of equal value.
Providing something to compensate for what another person lost is precisely what restitution means.
Most at home in courtrooms and formal writing, in collocations like pay restitution, make restitution, and restitution to the victims.
Do not confuse it with the sound-alike retribution, which means punishment or revenge; restitution repays a loss, while retribution inflicts one in return.

The community greenhouse on Alder Street was wrecked one October night: panes shattered, seed trays overturned, a season's work of the gardening club undone in an hour.
When two teenagers were caught on camera, the club asked the juvenile court for something other than jail.
The judge agreed and ordered full restitution: the pair would pay for every broken pane out of their own wages and rebuild the cedar benches they had kicked apart.
A donated check from a sympathetic stranger was declined; the club insisted the cost fall to the two who caused the loss.
By spring the glass was back, the benches stood again, and the ledger of the loss was closed by the people answerable for it.
